# 1 Samuel Chapter 31 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 168r–168v | **Source Image:** 1SA_031_page_001.jpg, 1SA_031_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Now the Philistines were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

**2** And the Philistines overtook Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan and Abinadab and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.

**3** The battle pressed hard against Saul, and the archers found him, and he was severely wounded by the archers.

**4** Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through and deal shamefully with me." But his armor-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell upon it.

**5** And when his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell upon his sword and died with him.

**6** So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, and all his men, on that same day together.

**7** And when the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley and those beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled. And the Philistines came and dwelt in them.

**8** On the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

**9** And they cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines, to carry the good news to the house of their idols and to the people.

**10** They put his armor in the temple of Ashtaroth, and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.

**11** But when the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,

**12** all the valiant men arose and walked all night and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan, and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.

**13** And they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

1. **31:2 — Jonathan's death**: Jonathan dies beside his father despite his loyalty to David. The narrative makes no comment on the injustice — it simply reports. Samuel's oracle ("you and your sons shall be with me," 28:19) is fulfilled without exception.

2. **31:3 — "severely wounded"**: The Hebrew va-yachel me'od may mean either "writhed in pain" or "trembled greatly." The ambiguity — physical and psychological anguish intertwined — captures Saul's state.

3. **31:4 — "deal shamefully"**: Hebrew hit'alelu — "make sport of, abuse." Saul's final concern is for his dignity. He chooses death by his own hand rather than humiliation at the hands of the uncircumcised.

4. **31:9 — "good news" (le-vasser)**: The root b-s-r (to bring news) is the same root behind "gospel." The Philistines proclaim Saul's death as their euangelion — victory news sent to their temples and people.

5. **31:11-13 — Jabesh-gilead's loyalty**: Saul's story ends where it began. He rescued Jabesh-gilead from the Ammonites (ch. 11); now its men risk everything to recover his body. This act of hesed — loyal love — provides the book's closing note of human dignity and faithfulness.

6. **31:13 — the tamarisk**: The same tree (eshel) under which Saul held court (22:6). His burial beneath a tamarisk creates a poignant literary echo — the tree of his power becomes the marker of his grave.

— LOGOS
